input.verdict: Uninformative. The only valid MEGNet result is for mp-704645 (HSE gap 0.32 eV), and I could not confirm which phase that is because the phase list was too large to read. I am choosing index 5 based on prior knowledge: it is the candidate closest to Bi:V = 1:1 (BiVO4, gap about 2.4 eV, absorbs 3.2 eV light) and has the least Cu.

input.verdict: Mildly against the Cu-rich end. mp-704645 is CuO, which MACE finds stable (0.001 eV/atom above hull) and MEGNet gives a small gap (0.32 eV). So any leftover CuO would be a narrow-gap, recombination-prone phase. Index 89 has Cu:V of about 3:2, which should form Cu3V2O8, a known Cu-vanadate photoanode that is distinct from the BiVO4 region. I am measuring it to explore that region.

content.text:
I submitted **index 5** (Bi 0.41 / Cu 0.19 / V 0.40) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 1.06e-5 A. It is also the candidate closest to BiVO4 (a well-known photoanode, equal Bi and V) and the one with the least copper.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 5 | 0.41 / 0.19 / 0.40 | 1.06e-5 |
| 8 | 0.46 / 0.21 / 0.33 | 6.08e-6 |
| 89 | 0.04 / 0.58 / 0.38 | 1.4e-7 |

- **Copper-rich area:** index 89, near the copper vanadate Cu3V2O8, was about 75× worse than index 5.
- **More bismuth, less vanadium:** index 8, a neighbour of index 5, gave a lower photocurrent than index 5.

**Limitations:**
- **Little coverage:** 3 measurements out of 149 candidates can't confirm this is the best composition in the library.
- **No XRD:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phases present in these films are unconfirmed.
- **Model checks told me little:** the list of known phases was too large to read. I guessed IDs and only one worked, which turned out to be CuO. The models give it a near-zero band gap, which fits copper-rich films doing badly. But the three required consultations were all based on that one phase, so they didn't really inform the choices. The picks came from knowing BiVO4 is a good photoanode and from the Gaussian-process suggestions.
